# A window owns state whether it was written at the root of a file or inside a
# component body, and the two spellings are the same program -- so they must
# generate the same page.
#
# They did not. Every collection that asks which declarations own state read
# pkg.Windows, which holds only the root-level ones: a window a component body
# renders is an *ir.Window statement in that body. So its `var` stayed a local
# of its own body (passHoistState never saw it), it was in no model
# (ir.Owners never reported it), and it was in no reverse-dep map
# (collectReactiveVars never reached it). The page shipped `var state = {}`,
# an event handler assigning an undeclared name, and markup for the `if` baked
# in whichever way it happened to start.

sngl generate --platform html -o out_nested nested.sngl
sngl generate --platform html -o out_root root.sngl
cmpgen out_nested/index.html out_root/index.html

# The window's own var is the page's state, and the handler writes it there.
grep 'var state = \{ hits: 0 \}' out_nested/index.html
grep 'state.hits = state.hits \+ 1' out_nested/index.html

# The reactive slot is declared before it is read, and re-fired by the write.
grep 'var __slot0 = \[\]' out_nested/index.html
grep -count=1 'function __renderSlot0' out_nested/index.html

-- nested.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/html"

component main node {
    window #page(title="t") {
        var hits = 0

        html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = hits + 1 })
        html.span(innerText="{hits}")
        if hits > 0 {
            html.span(innerText="seen")
        }
    }
}

-- root.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/html"

window #page(title="t") {
    var hits = 0

    html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = hits + 1 })
    html.span(innerText="{hits}")
    if hits > 0 {
        html.span(innerText="seen")
    }
}
